description:
Did You Know Old TV Static Showed the Big Bang?

A small part of the static on old analog TVs came from the cosmic microwave background, light released 380,000 years after the Big Bang. It was discovered by accident in 1965.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

#bigbang #space #science #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: If you ever saw static on an old TV, you saw a little bit of the Big Bang.
When an old TV couldn't find a channel, it showed snowy static.
segments.headline: TV snow

segments.text: About one percent of that static was a signal from the beginning of the universe.
It's called the cosmic microwave background. Light released about three hundred and eighty thousand years after the Big Bang.
segments.headline: The oldest light

segments.text: It has been travelling for thirteen point eight billion years to reach you.
It was found by accident in 1965. Two radio engineers kept hearing a hiss in their antenna. They even cleaned out pigeon droppings to get rid of it.
segments.headline: Blame the pigeons?

segments.text: The hiss didn't go away. It was the Big Bang. They won a Nobel Prize for it.
Next stop: The Speed of Light. Do you remember TV static? Tell me how old you are in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
